question: A 22-year-old man with extensive KOH-confirmed tinea corporis has not responded to 4 weeks of oral terbinafine 250 mg/day. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Switch to oral itraconazole, suspecting terbinafine-resistant dermatophytosis, and stop any steroid-containing combination creams

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. KOH-confirmed tinea that fails adequate terbinafine in the Indian setting should raise suspicion for squalene epoxidase mutations in the T. mentagrophytes/indotineae complex. Itraconazole targets a different enzyme (lanosterol 14-α-demethylase) and is the standard switch. Stopping steroid-antifungal combination creams is essential as they drive tinea incognito.

answers.text: Add a potent topical steroid-antifungal combination cream to settle the inflammation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Steroid-containing combination creams are a major driver of the chronic dermatophytosis epidemic in India. They suppress itch temporarily but spread the infection, mask the diagnostic active border (tinea incognito), and worsen long-term outcomes.

answers.text: Repeat the same terbinafine course for another 4 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. If an adequate terbinafine course has failed in a KOH-positive case, repeating the same regimen ignores the likely squalene epoxidase mutation. A class switch to itraconazole is more rational than re-challenging with the same failing agent.

answers.text: Stop all antifungals and conclude the diagnosis is incorrect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The diagnosis is confirmed by KOH demonstrating septate branching hyphae. Treatment failure in a confirmed case reflects drug resistance, not diagnostic error — a switch to a different antifungal class is warranted.

overallFeedback.feedback: When KOH-confirmed tinea fails terbinafine, suspect squalene epoxidase mutations and switch to itraconazole — do not repeat, add steroids, or doubt the confirmed diagnosis.
Recognising terbinafine resistance and switching to itraconazole is a critical management skill in the Indian dermatophytosis epidemic.
